figureLabel: Clay modelling, beads and collage with Ghana flag colours
altText: KG2 children moulding clay farm tools, rolling paper beads and building a large Ghana flag collage with red, yellow and green scraps.
detailedDescription: In a KG2 classroom, small groups of learners rotate between three tables. At one table, children mould simple farm tools like hoes and cutlasses from clay and later paint them in bright colours. At another, they roll strips of old calendars and brown paper into beads and string them into necklaces. At the third table, learners glue red, yellow and green paper pieces onto a large sheet to form a Ghana flag collage. The teacher moves around asking how the tools are used, what colours they see in the flag and encouraging learners to talk positively about one another’s creations.

figureLabel: Family tree collage with 2D and 3D elements
altText: KG2 learners designing a family tree collage using cut-out shapes, small photos and raised paper pieces to make a mix of two- and three-dimensional artwork.
detailedDescription: On a wide sheet of drawing paper labelled "My Family Tree", KG2 learners cut and paste simple shapes to form a big tree trunk and branches. They glue small photos or drawings of family members on the branches and add raised paper pieces or cardboard frames so that some parts stand out in low relief. Children write the initial letters of each family member’s name under the pictures. When they finish, pairs of learners show each other their family trees and talk about who is in their family and why they chose particular colours and shapes.

figureLabel: Greeting cards and artworks discussion circle
altText: KG2 children sitting in a circle examining greeting cards and pictures of lights while talking about how the artworks were made.
detailedDescription: In a discussion circle, KG2 learners each hold a different greeting card or printed picture of natural and man-made lights. The teacher invites one child at a time to show their card, describe the colours and shapes they see and guess how the card was made, for example by drawing, painting or printing. Some learners notice glitter or cut-and-paste textures. The teacher models phrases like "I think the artist used..." and connects the conversation to showing good manners, such as using cards to say "thank you" or "get well soon".

figureLabel: Patterns and uses of plants in the environment
altText: KG2 learners looking at a poster showing rows of trees, leaves and garden beds while discussing patterns and the many uses of plants.
detailedDescription: Using a large conversational poster, the teacher points out repeated rows of trees, leaves and flower beds in a school or community scene. KG2 learners notice patterns such as alternating light and dark leaves or evenly spaced trees along a path. They also talk about how plants give shade, food and medicine. Some children trace the repeated shapes with their fingers in the air, while others try drawing similar patterns on small sheets of paper, linking visual patterns with real-life uses of plants.

altText: KG2 classroom wall displaying drawings of living and non-living things while children point and talk about the ideas in the artworks.
detailedDescription: Along one wall of the KG2 classroom, drawings are displayed in two sections: "Living Things" and "Non-living Things". Learners have drawn items such as trees, goats and children under the living section and stones, houses and cars under the non-living section. During gallery time, children stand in front of the display, classify a few of the pictures, count how many are in each group and explain the ideas behind their own drawings. The teacher prompts them to use words like "moves", "grows" and "does not grow" to talk about the differences.

figureLabel: Describing colour and shape in everyday objects
altText: KG2 learners pointing to trees, buildings and dresses on a poster while naming colours and shapes they can see.
detailedDescription: In front of a large poster showing a school compound, KG2 learners take turns pointing to objects such as trees, walls, roofs and clothes. They describe them using colour words like red, yellow, green, white and black, and sometimes mention simple shapes like round, square or tall and thin. The teacher writes some of the colour words on strips of card and matches them to items on the poster. Learners begin to see that the environment is full of organised elements of art such as colour, line and shape.

figureLabel: Creating simple repeating patterns with colour and size
altText: KG2 children arranging coloured paper strips into repeating patterns and then drawing their favourite parts.
detailedDescription: On a low table, KG2 learners arrange coloured paper strips or shape cards into simple repeating patterns such as red-blue-red-blue or small-big-small-big. After building their patterns, they glue them onto paper to make borders or simple designs. Some children then draw and colour their favourite part of the pattern and explain to a partner what they like about it. The teacher extends the activity by clapping short sound patterns that the class echoes, linking visual and rhythmic pattern-making.

figureLabel: Talking about weather pictures and everyday art
altText: KG2 learners discussing pictures of sunny, rainy and cloudy weather and using simple weather words in sentences.
detailedDescription: The teacher displays a set of pictures showing sunny, rainy, cloudy and windy weather above a scene of a Ghanaian town. KG2 learners talk about the beauty of each scene, noticing colours in the sky, clothing and umbrellas. They use simple vocabulary such as "sunny day", "heavy rain" and "cool wind" to make short oral sentences. The teacher helps them see that posters, calendars and even shop signs are everyday artworks that carry information about weather and daily life.

figureLabel: Art inspired by palace and cultural symbols
altText: KG2 children studying a picture of a traditional palace and then drawing and labelling a colourful royal umbrella.
detailedDescription: Using a clear picture of a traditional Ghanaian palace, the teacher guides KG2 learners to notice features such as the royal umbrella, carved doors and decorated walls. Children talk briefly about which parts they like. Afterwards they draw a large umbrella on paper, decorate it with bright patterns and label it with a simple word like "umbrella" or the name of the chief’s town. Some learners also add small flags or drums around their umbrellas, showing how cultural places can inspire new artworks.

figureLabel: Patriotic song, improvised instruments and march past
altText: KG2 learners marching and dancing to a patriotic Ghanaian song while some play improvised drums and shakers.
detailedDescription: Outside on a clean field, KG2 learners practise a simple march past to a recording of a patriotic Ghanaian song such as "Hɛn ara asaase ni". A few children play improvised instruments made from tins, plastic bottles and seeds, keeping a steady beat while others march, swing their arms and sing along. Before or after the march, the teacher explains key words from the song and briefly links the activity to loving and caring for Ghana. The scene shows how music, dance and movement can communicate history and national pride even with simple, low-cost resources.
